newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks slip in thin trade, but CANTV ahead.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks slip in thin trade, but CANTV ahead.

text.p: Caracas stocks slipped in thin trade as investor interest waned, traders said, although shares in telephone company CANTV took heart on news rates would rise 20 percent in January.
"The only stock that attracted any interest today was CANTV," said Profimerca broker Miguel Gonzalez.
CANTV gained 50.00 bolivars to end at 1795.00.

Despite the bolsa's droop, traders said the 2.89 percent fall in the index to 5,986.35 points was overstated on a price adjustment by Banco Mercantil after increasing its capital with a one-for-two share issue.
Banco Mercantil A Series shares closed at 1,825.00 bolivars after ending last night at 2,700.00. Its B shares closed at 1,414.00 bolivars after Monday's 2,140.00 close.
Among traded issues, 27 fell, eight rose, six closed flat as 12.59 million shares traded worth 3.5 billion bolivars ($7.4 million).
"It was a terrible session, dead," said one trader.
"Some think the bolsa will surge at the end of the year on the Banco de Venezuela and Consolidado sales, but if CANTV didn't set it roaring, I don't see why banks should," he added.
